title: KV cache corruption escalation - remediation & postmortem plan
summary: Follow-up on intermittent KV cache corruption observed during the 2025-05-05 outage window. Review of root cause candidate, short-term mitigations, long-term fixes, SLA/credits discussion, and timeline for postmortem writeup and regression test plan.
topics: Root cause hypothesis (cache eviction + compaction bug)

Redwood SE to run deterministic KV exercise with DataForge week of 5/12
Customer to share failing prompts and sample payloads by 5/9
Schedule follow-up technical deep dive (30m) on 5/14

transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-05-07 16:38 UTC | Duration: ~50m | Recording ID: ff-20250507-1638-kvcache
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Maya Singh (Redwood SE), Luca Romano (Redwood SRE), Jordan Park (Redwood CSM); Priya Rao (DataForge VP Eng), Evan Brooks (DataForge SRE Lead), Samir Patel (DataForge Platform Eng), Jules Martin (DataForge Security)

[00:00] Avery Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining on short notice. We wanted to make sure we had a focused follow-up to the outage on Monday, go over what we know, and agree next steps. Priya, can I hand it to you for a quick summary from the DataForge side?

[00:22] Priya Rao: Yeah, thanks Avery. So Monday morning we saw a spike in 5xxs from the inference tier starting around 09:12 local. It recovered after we rolled the instance pool but we noticed some downstream generation artifacts — duplicated tokens and truncation — and some users reported data leakage like stale responses for unrelated tenants. Not all requests were affected but it was enough to cause an incident and an escalation.

[01:05] Evan Brooks: For us the first signal was a mismatch between cache hits and observed latency; the KV cache reported hits but the model produced out-of-context completions. We correlated it to a compaction job that ran around 09:10.

[01:25] Maya Singh: Thanks, that matches Redwood telemetry. We observed an increase in KV error logs and a brief period where the cache index reported inconsistent entries. There were also a handful of aborted writes to the local cache that coincide with compaction.

[02:05] Jules Martin: From security, we were worried about the stale responses being served across tenants. We have not seen evidence of cross-tenant data exfiltration in persistent storage yet, but the appearance of stale state in outputs is concerning.

[02:30] Luca Romano: Quick framing from SRE: our initial hypothesis is a race during compaction + eviction where in-memory index pointers were momentarily inconsistent. That can cause reads to surface old or wrong KV entries until heal completes. It's intermittent, explains partial impact.

[03:00] Priya Rao: Do you think this is an algorithmic bug or something triggered by load? We were under normal traffic but with a higher-than-usual tail due to a marketing burst.

[03:18] Maya Singh: It's likely both. The compaction path had a regression in the eviction ordering introduced in the quantization-compat optim branch. Under normal traffic it shouldn't fail, but with tail spikes the timing window widened and exposed the race.

[03:45] Samir Patel: Can you point to commit or PR that introduced the regression? We have compliance requirements to track changes that impact data integrity.

[03:58] Maya Singh: We're tracking it to PR #3782 in the runtime repo — the change adjusted compaction scheduling and didn't cover a pointer swap case. We missed a codepath in unit tests.

[04:18] Evan Brooks: What's the blast radius? Were only some model variants affected? We run mixed Llama-2 forks and a few quantized layers.

[04:30] Luca Romano: Early read of logs indicates the issue surfaced on the quantized x8 paths primarily — the pointer swap is in the compaction logic used by that codepath. Hosted non-quantized replicas saw fewer anomalies. That said, we saw anomalies across a handful of tenants because those tenants were on the same physical pool.

[04:56] Priya Rao: For our legal/compliance team, can we confirm whether persisted logs contain any user content duplication between tenants?

[05:12] Jordan Park: We haven't found evidence of persisted cross-tenant content in object storage. The symptoms were primarily at the in-memory cache and transient responses. We'll of course escalate if we find anything else.

[05:35] Jules Martin: Please be explicit about that in the postmortem; our auditors will want clear language.

[05:46] Avery Chen: Understood. Let's walk through mitigations. Luca, what immediate mitigation can Redwood perform to prevent recurrence while we patch?

[06:00] Luca Romano: Short term we can disable concurrent compaction on impacted pools and force compaction to run during low-traffic windows. That reduces throughput a bit, maybe 5-10% CPU overhead, but removes the race. We can also shift affected tenants to a compatible non-quantized replica flavor as a hotfix.

[06:26] Samir Patel: How disruptive is shifting tenants? Can that happen with zero downtime?

[06:32] Maya Singh: We can do a rolling migration: spin up non-quantized replicas, warm caches, then drain traffic. For most customers it's 1-2 minutes per replica, no broad downtime, but it will increase cost during the window.

[06:50] Priya Rao: We need to know cost impact; we can't just incur surprise charges.

[06:56] Avery Chen: We'll include cost delta in the follow-up. Also, we should consider SLA credits. Jordan, can you give a quick take?

[07:06] Jordan Park: From the contract, DataForge is in a tier with a 99.9% availability SLA for inference. The incident window resulted in about 48 minutes of degraded responses across a subset of requests — we estimate credit applies for affected tenant hours. I'll propose a credit number and include the calculation in the postmortem.

[07:30] Priva Rao: Please share the math. We will need it for the finance team.

[07:36] Jordan Park: Will do.

[07:40] Evan Brooks: On recovery, you mentioned aborted writes. How confident are you that we didn't lose any user state or cause KV divergence that persists?

[07:52] Luca Romano: The aborted writes were not persisted to durable storage; they were GC'd during a later reconcile pass, so we believe durable state is intact. The risk was in-memory pointers returning stale entries. Our reconcile fixed most entries automatically. We're running a targeted consistency check to validate across the pool.

[08:18] Maya Singh: We're also going to add a deterministic KV replay that replays writes from the prior 24h window into a validation cluster to ensure no shadow state diverged. That's one of the action items.

[08:35] Samir Patel: Ok if you run the replay we can validate responses from our side and give signoff. We'll share sample payloads.

[08:44] Priya Rao: Timeframe for the patch?

[08:48] Maya Singh: We have a proposed fix for the pointer swap today; unit tests updated. We need a couple days for integration testing and a controlled canary rollout. So target patch to prod by Friday 5/09, pending validation.

[09:02] Evan Brooks: Are you confident no other codepaths have similar races?

[09:07] Luca Romano: We'll run a grep-based audit for similar compaction/ejection code and expand fuzzing. But given the change set is narrow, we think the regression is isolated. We'll also add a race-detection job to CI for the compaction path.

[09:28] Priya Rao: We'll need an independent verification step. Our SRE wants to run a deterministic test harness against the canary.

[09:36] Maya Singh: Absolutely. We'll share access to a canary cluster and run the harness together. That's in the next steps.

[09:45] Jules Martin: One compliance question — do you have an audit trail in the control plane for compaction jobs and their parameters? For us we need retention of config changes and who triggered them.

[09:57] Luca Romano: Yes, control plane logs store compaction job triggers, config snapshots, and the operator ID. We'll export the relevant logs for the window and attach to the postmortem.

[10:12] Priya Rao: OK. For the postmortem writeup, we want clear timelines, root cause, remediation, what changed in our contracts if anything, and a mitigation checklist.

[10:22] Avery Chen: We'll deliver that. Jordan will own the timeline and credit calculation; Maya and Luca will own technical root cause and repair; Samir will validate with sample payloads. We'll share a draft by 2025-05-12 and then publish a joint postmortem.

[10:36] Evan Brooks: Any legal escalation? Our privacy team is watching but no PII leakage so far.

[10:42] Jules Martin: We'll continue to monitor but will escalate if evidence arises.

[10:48] Maya Singh: Two quick asks: one, can DataForge provide the list of affected tenant IDs and example request IDs so we can correlate logs? Two, can you approve a maintenance window Friday night for the patch deployment?

[11:05] Samir Patel: We'll share tenant IDs and request IDs by tomorrow EOD. For the maintenance window, Friday night is fine but we need a precise UTC window.

[11:15] Avery Chen: We'll propose 2025-05-09 02:00-04:00 UTC as the window in the follow-up email.

[11:22] Priya Rao: Fine. Also include rollback plan and who to call if we see any regressions.

[11:30] Luca Romano: Rollback is immediate flip to previous runtime image and re-enable concurrent compaction; rollback should be < 5 minutes per shard. We'll provide runbook steps and POC contacts.

[11:40] Evan Brooks: Good. On monitoring improvements, can we get a new metric for compaction pointer swap rate or at least a compaction error counter?

[11:49] Maya Singh: Yes we'll add an aggregated compaction anomaly metric and an alert threshold for any non-zero error in production. That will be in the postmortem action list.

[12:00] Priya Rao: Great. Let's recap next steps and owners.

[12:05] Avery Chen: Recap: Redwood to provide postmortem draft by 5/12 (Jordan); proposed patch by 5/09 (Maya/Luca) with canary access for DataForge SREs (Evan/Samir) to validate; tenant/request IDs and payloads from DataForge by 5/09 (Samir); SLA credit proposal (Avery/Jordan) by 5/09; maintenance window confirmation and rollback runbook (Luca) included in follow-up.

[12:35] Priya Rao: That aligns. We expect frequent updates in the channel. Please flag any change in timeline.

[12:44] Avery Chen: Thanks everyone. We'll send notes and tasks after the call. If anything new emerges please DM Jules or Jordan immediately.

[12:52] Jules Martin: Thanks.

[13:00] Meeting ends.

Notes: transcript contains a few mis-hearings in auto captions; proper nouns may be slightly off. References: PR #3782, runtime repo, compaction job logs (to be attached).
